narrative.overview:
EPS Digital's visual language is a study in restrained confidence. The system speaks with the authority of a trusted healthcare provider — calm, clear, and unwavering — while avoiding the cold sterility that plagues medical software. Every surface earns its place through utility, not decoration. The deep navy (#2B3E59) anchors the entire experience like the sturdy frame of a clinic door: always visible, never ornamental.

The palette is deliberately limited. A single strong primary carries the brand weight across navbars, buttons, and section headers, while a carefully graded neutral scale handles the rest. White backgrounds keep the airiness that patients need when navigating health concerns. Color appears with purpose — green for availability, red for errors, blue-200 for emphasis in hero text — never as filler.

Layout is generous and uncluttered. The 1440px max-width container, 24px padding, and 24px grid gaps create breathing room that respects the user's attention. Cards are the primary content vessel: rounded-xl, softly shadowed, always on white. The system favors full-width CTAs and hero sections that let the brand gradient speak.
keyCharacteristics: Navy-anchored calm: the primary #2B3E59 appears on every key surface, creating instant recognition
White-dominant backgrounds with soft #F5F5F5 page tint for depth contrast
Generous whitespace: 24px internal padding, 16-24px gaps, max-width 1440px container
Rounded-full CTAs as the signature interactive pattern (pill-shaped buttons)
Inter headings for authority, Roboto body for readability
Minimal shadow vocabulary: ambient lifts only, never structural blocks
Healthcare-appropriate restraint: no gradients on text, no glass effects, no decorative flourishes

rules.name: The Navy Anchor Rule
rules.body: The primary navy (#2B3E59) appears on every key interactive surface — navbar, sidebar, primary buttons, section headings. Its omnipresence is the brand signature.

rules.name: The White Space Doctrine
rules.body: Backgrounds are white or page-tint (#F5F5F5). No card, section, or content area uses a saturated or tinted background unless it is a branded gradient banner.

rules.name: The Heading Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings use Inter at 600-700 weight. Body text and labels use Roboto at 400-500. Never mix.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only to signal interactivity (hover) or layering (modal, dropdown).

dos: Do use navy (#2B3E59) as the primary accent on every key interactive surface
Do keep backgrounds white or page-tint (#F5F5F5)
Do use rounded-full (pill) shapes for primary and secondary CTA buttons
Do pair Inter for headings with Roboto for body
Do use 24px internal padding and 24px grid gaps as the standard spacing rhythm
Do keep shadows minimal — ambient lifts for cards at rest, slightly deeper on hover
Do use the navy gradient (135deg, #2B3E59 → #3a527a) for hero sections and CTA banners
donts: Don't use saturated or tinted backgrounds for content cards
Don't add gradient text, glass effects, or decorative blur
Don't use hard-offset shadows (box-shadow: 4px 4px 0) or block shadows
Don't put section numbers or eyebrow kickers above headings
Don't use rounded-xl on buttons or rounded-full on cards
Don't apply color to text labels or secondary copy for decoration
Don't use modals for tasks that don't require interruption or protected focus
